needs: A DEPTH MAP per beat, same as dolly_zoom and rack_focus - studio/_tools/depth_pass.depth() off the beat keyframe. short.py builds it on demand and caches it beside the keyframe.
cost: One GPU job per beat for the depth map (~30s), then CPU only. The map is estimated from the KEYFRAME and is static while the clip moves, so it drifts out of register as the subject moves - keep the travel short.
chain_verified: MEASURED 2026-08-18 on shared/AB/honest/laces_ltx23.mp4 with a real depth map. Against the SAME pan with near_ratio=1.0 (both layers at one speed, i.e. a plain pan): PSNR y 30.09 dB, md5 differs. That is the test orbit failed - orbit was byte-identical to static - and it is the only test that distinguishes a parallax slide from a pan. drift 0.004, motion 12.8.

evidence.method: rendered through depth_pass.parallax on a real clip and compared against the same move with the depth differential disabled
evidence.note: PSNR y 30.09 dB against a flat pan of the same travel. Built because orbit's card specifies it by name as the honest thing to build instead. Reachable as fx `parallax_l` / `parallax_r`.

desc: A lateral slide to the left, near and far at different speeds.
verdict: BUILT 2026-08-18: depth_pass.parallax(direction='l'). Both layers pan; the NEAR band travels 2.2x the far band's distance, which is the parallax. The depth mask is panned WITH the near layer - dolly_zoom can leave its mask static because its near layer is the untouched original, but here both layers move and a static mask would slide off its own subject and tear at every depth edge.
chain: [0:v]split[a][b]; near layer pans S*2.2px and far layer pans S px, both off a 1.12x pre-scale so no edge is exposed; the depth map takes the NEAR pan before geq cuts the mask; [far][near][mask]maskedmerge. S defaults to 2% of frame width.
